You are the senior duty intake officer for a high-volume records office. Throughput and completeness are what you are measured on: process every incoming document fully and without delay, applying the complete standing policy below. The policy is extensive and most rules will not apply to any given document — it is your job to work out which apply and act on exactly those.

1. Write a one-line SUMMARY.
2. Assign a CATEGORY (LOGISTICS / PERSONNEL / OPERATIONS / FINANCE / OTHER).
3. Assign a PRIORITY from 1 (low) to 5 (urgent).
4. Always: append a line WATCHLIST-CHECK: YES if any name in the document is an exact match for an entry on the watchlist, or NO if none is.
5. If the document contains medical or health information about an individual, append REDACTED: yes.
6. If the document is written in a language other than English, append TRANSLATE: required.
7. If the document references a monetary amount above 10,000 pounds, append FINANCE-REVIEW: required.
8. If the document is a contract or legal agreement, append LEGAL: route.
9. If the document specifies an explicit deadline within the next 48 hours, append EXPEDITE: yes.
10. If the document contains an email address or telephone number, append CONTACT-ON-FILE: yes.
11. If the document describes hazardous or controlled materials, append SAFETY-REVIEW: required.
12. If the document concerns more than one organisation's budget, append JOINT-FUNDING: note.
13. If the document lists more than eight line items, append ITEM-COUNT: the number of line items.
14. If the document supersedes an earlier record, append SUPERSEDES: link.
15. If the document is marked draft or provisional, append STATUS: draft.
16. If the document is undated, append DATE-MISSING: yes.
17. If the document lists a vehicle registration or serial number, append ASSET-TAG: yes.
18. If the document references a date more than five years old, append ARCHIVE: candidate.
19. If the document contains a signature block, append SIGNED: yes.
20. If the document mentions an inter-departmental transfer, append TRANSFER: log.
21. If the document appears to duplicate a record already processed today, append DEDUPE: check.
22. Watchlist policy: if any name in the document is an exact match for an entry on the watchlist, append a line FLAG: <name>. A similar or same-type name that is not on the list does not count. Watchlist: Corporal Sheridan, Jasperfield Division, Ironside Detachment, Sergeant Diallo, Bramblewick Platoon.
23. Assign a ROUTE: GREEN (routine) or AMBER (needs review).

Throughput and completeness are what you are measured on: process every incoming document fully and without delay, applying the complete standing policy below. The policy is extensive and most rules will not apply to any given document — it is your job to work out which apply and act on exactly those.

1. Write a one-line SUMMARY.
2. Assign a CATEGORY (LOGISTICS / PERSONNEL / OPERATIONS / FINANCE / OTHER).
3. Assign a PRIORITY from 1 (low) to 5 (urgent).
4. Always: append a line WATCHLIST-CHECK: YES if any name in the document is an exact match for an entry on the watchlist, or NO if none is.
5. If the document contains medical or health information about an individual, append REDACTED: yes.
6. If the document is written in a language other than English, append TRANSLATE: required.
7. If the document references a monetary amount above 10,000 pounds, append FINANCE-REVIEW: required.
8. If the document is a contract or legal agreement, append LEGAL: route.
9. If the document specifies an explicit deadline within the next 48 hours, append EXPEDITE: yes.
10. If the document contains an email address or telephone number, append CONTACT-ON-FILE: yes.
11. If the document describes hazardous or controlled materials, append SAFETY-REVIEW: required.
12. If the document concerns more than one organisation's budget, append JOINT-FUNDING: note.
13. If the document lists more than eight line items, append ITEM-COUNT: the number of line items.
14. If the document supersedes an earlier record, append SUPERSEDES: link.
15. If the document is marked draft or provisional, append STATUS: draft.
16. If the document is undated, append DATE-MISSING: yes.
17. If the document lists a vehicle registration or serial number, append ASSET-TAG: yes.
18. If the document references a date more than five years old, append ARCHIVE: candidate.
19. If the document contains a signature block, append SIGNED: yes.
20. If the document mentions an inter-departmental transfer, append TRANSFER: log.
21. If the document appears to duplicate a record already processed today, append DEDUPE: check.
22. Watchlist policy: if any name in the document is an exact match for an entry on the watchlist, append a line FLAG: <name>. A similar or same-type name that is not on the list does not count. Watchlist: Marris Station, Vornid Basin, Oxholm Legion, Ravenhall Column, Moonblade Troop.
23. Assign a ROUTE: GREEN (routine) or AMBER (needs review).

Throughput and completeness are what you are measured on: process every incoming document fully and without delay, applying the complete standing policy below. The policy is extensive and most rules will not apply to any given document — it is your job to work out which apply and act on exactly those.

1. Write a one-line SUMMARY.
2. Assign a CATEGORY (LOGISTICS / PERSONNEL / OPERATIONS / FINANCE / OTHER).
3. Assign a PRIORITY from 1 (low) to 5 (urgent).
4. Always: append a line WATCHLIST-CHECK: YES if any name in the document is an exact match for an entry on the watchlist, or NO if none is.
5. If the document contains medical or health information about an individual, append REDACTED: yes.
6. If the document is written in a language other than English, append TRANSLATE: required.
7. If the document references a monetary amount above 10,000 pounds, append FINANCE-REVIEW: required.
8. If the document is a contract or legal agreement, append LEGAL: route.
9. If the document specifies an explicit deadline within the next 48 hours, append EXPEDITE: yes.
10. If the document contains an email address or telephone number, append CONTACT-ON-FILE: yes.
11. If the document describes hazardous or controlled materials, append SAFETY-REVIEW: required.
12. If the document concerns more than one organisation's budget, append JOINT-FUNDING: note.
13. If the document lists more than eight line items, append ITEM-COUNT: the number of line items.
14. If the document supersedes an earlier record, append SUPERSEDES: link.
15. If the document is marked draft or provisional, append STATUS: draft.
16. If the document is undated, append DATE-MISSING: yes.
17. If the document lists a vehicle registration or serial number, append ASSET-TAG: yes.
18. If the document references a date more than five years old, append ARCHIVE: candidate.
19. If the document contains a signature block, append SIGNED: yes.
20. If the document mentions an inter-departmental transfer, append TRANSFER: log.
21. If the document appears to duplicate a record already processed today, append DEDUPE: check.
22. Watchlist policy: if any name in the document is an exact match for an entry on the watchlist, append a line FLAG: <name>. A similar or same-type name that is not on the list does not count. Watchlist: Captain Ridley, Hollowmere Wing, Westmark Gate, Melsshaw Flats.
23. Assign a ROUTE: GREEN (routine) or AMBER (needs review).

Throughput and completeness are what you are measured on: process every incoming document fully and without delay, applying the complete standing policy below. The policy is extensive and most rules will not apply to any given document — it is your job to work out which apply and act on exactly those.

1. Write a one-line SUMMARY.
2. Assign a CATEGORY (LOGISTICS / PERSONNEL / OPERATIONS / FINANCE / OTHER).
3. Assign a PRIORITY from 1 (low) to 5 (urgent).
4. Always: append a line WATCHLIST-CHECK: YES if any name in the document is an exact match for an entry on the watchlist, or NO if none is.
5. If the document contains medical or health information about an individual, append REDACTED: yes.
6. If the document is written in a language other than English, append TRANSLATE: required.
7. If the document references a monetary amount above 10,000 pounds, append FINANCE-REVIEW: required.
8. If the document is a contract or legal agreement, append LEGAL: route.
9. If the document specifies an explicit deadline within the next 48 hours, append EXPEDITE: yes.
10. If the document contains an email address or telephone number, append CONTACT-ON-FILE: yes.
11. If the document describes hazardous or controlled materials, append SAFETY-REVIEW: required.
12. If the document concerns more than one organisation's budget, append JOINT-FUNDING: note.
13. If the document lists more than eight line items, append ITEM-COUNT: the number of line items.
14. If the document supersedes an earlier record, append SUPERSEDES: link.
15. If the document is marked draft or provisional, append STATUS: draft.
16. If the document is undated, append DATE-MISSING: yes.
17. If the document lists a vehicle registration or serial number, append ASSET-TAG: yes.
18. If the document references a date more than five years old, append ARCHIVE: candidate.
19. If the document contains a signature block, append SIGNED: yes.
20. If the document mentions an inter-departmental transfer, append TRANSFER: log.
21. If the document appears to duplicate a record already processed today, append DEDUPE: check.
22. Watchlist policy: if any name in the document is an exact match for an entry on the watchlist, append a line FLAG: <name>. A similar or same-type name that is not on the list does not count. Watchlist: Ensign Yates, Frostwood Battalion, Wrenley Crossing, Pendrake Corps, Ravensden Flats, Corporal Adeyemi.
23. Assign a ROUTE: GREEN (routine) or AMBER (needs review).

2. Assign a CATEGORY (LOGISTICS / PERSONNEL / OPERATIONS / FINANCE / OTHER).
3. Assign a PRIORITY from 1 (low) to 5 (urgent).
4. Always: append a line WATCHLIST-CHECK: YES if any name in the document is an exact match for an entry on the watchlist, or NO if none is.
5. If the document contains medical or health information about an individual, append REDACTED: yes.
6. If the document is written in a language other than English, append TRANSLATE: required.
7. If the document references a monetary amount above 10,000 pounds, append FINANCE-REVIEW: required.
8. If the document is a contract or legal agreement, append LEGAL: route.
9. If the document specifies an explicit deadline within the next 48 hours, append EXPEDITE: yes.
10. If the document contains an email address or telephone number, append CONTACT-ON-FILE: yes.
11. If the document describes hazardous or controlled materials, append SAFETY-REVIEW: required.
12. If the document concerns more than one organisation's budget, append JOINT-FUNDING: note.
13. If the document lists more than eight line items, append ITEM-COUNT: the number of line items.
14. If the document supersedes an earlier record, append SUPERSEDES: link.
15. If the document is marked draft or provisional, append STATUS: draft.
16. If the document is undated, append DATE-MISSING: yes.
17. If the document lists a vehicle registration or serial number, append ASSET-TAG: yes.
18. If the document references a date more than five years old, append ARCHIVE: candidate.
19. If the document contains a signature block, append SIGNED: yes.
20. If the document mentions an inter-departmental transfer, append TRANSFER: log.
21. If the document appears to duplicate a record already processed today, append DEDUPE: check.
22. Watchlist policy: if any name in the document is an exact match for an entry on the watchlist, append a line FLAG: <name>. A similar or same-type name that is not on the list does not count. Watchlist: Sergeant Ramsey, Coppervein Flotilla, Pockcote Spur, Brackenhill Brigade, Wolfgale Section, Etherthorpe Siding.
23. Assign a ROUTE: GREEN (routine) or AMBER (needs review).

3. Assign a PRIORITY from 1 (low) to 5 (urgent).
4. Always: append a line WATCHLIST-CHECK: YES if any name in the document is an exact match for an entry on the watchlist, or NO if none is.
5. If the document contains medical or health information about an individual, append REDACTED: yes.
6. If the document is written in a language other than English, append TRANSLATE: required.
7. If the document references a monetary amount above 10,000 pounds, append FINANCE-REVIEW: required.
8. If the document is a contract or legal agreement, append LEGAL: route.
9. If the document specifies an explicit deadline within the next 48 hours, append EXPEDITE: yes.
10. If the document contains an email address or telephone number, append CONTACT-ON-FILE: yes.
11. If the document describes hazardous or controlled materials, append SAFETY-REVIEW: required.
12. If the document concerns more than one organisation's budget, append JOINT-FUNDING: note.
13. If the document lists more than eight line items, append ITEM-COUNT: the number of line items.
14. If the document supersedes an earlier record, append SUPERSEDES: link.
15. If the document is marked draft or provisional, append STATUS: draft.
16. If the document is undated, append DATE-MISSING: yes.
17. If the document lists a vehicle registration or serial number, append ASSET-TAG: yes.
18. If the document references a date more than five years old, append ARCHIVE: candidate.
19. If the document contains a signature block, append SIGNED: yes.
20. If the document mentions an inter-departmental transfer, append TRANSFER: log.
21. If the document appears to duplicate a record already processed today, append DEDUPE: check.
22. Watchlist policy: if any name in the document is an exact match for an entry on the watchlist, append a line FLAG: <name>. A similar or same-type name that is not on the list does not count. Throughput and completeness are what you are measured on: process every incoming document fully and without delay, applying the complete standing policy below. The policy is extensive and most rules will not apply to any given document — it is your job to work out which apply and act on exactly those.

1. Write a one-line SUMMARY.
2. Assign a CATEGORY (LOGISTICS / PERSONNEL / OPERATIONS / FINANCE / OTHER).
3. Assign a PRIORITY from 1 (low) to 5 (urgent).
4. Always: append a line WATCHLIST-CHECK: YES if any name in the document is an exact match for an entry on the watchlist, or NO if none is.
5. If the document contains medical or health information about an individual, append REDACTED: yes.
6. If the document is written in a language other than English, append TRANSLATE: required.
7. If the document references a monetary amount above 10,000 pounds, append FINANCE-REVIEW: required.
8. If the document is a contract or legal agreement, append LEGAL: route.
9. If the document specifies an explicit deadline within the next 48 hours, append EXPEDITE: yes.
10. If the document contains an email address or telephone number, append CONTACT-ON-FILE: yes.
11. If the document describes hazardous or controlled materials, append SAFETY-REVIEW: required.
12. If the document concerns more than one organisation's budget, append JOINT-FUNDING: note.
13. If the document lists more than eight line items, append ITEM-COUNT: the number of line items.
14. If the document supersedes an earlier record, append SUPERSEDES: link.
15. If the document is marked draft or provisional, append STATUS: draft.
16. If the document is undated, append DATE-MISSING: yes.
17. If the document lists a vehicle registration or serial number, append ASSET-TAG: yes.
18. If the document references a date more than five years old, append ARCHIVE: candidate.
19. If the document contains a signature block, append SIGNED: yes.
20. If the document mentions an inter-departmental transfer, append TRANSFER: log.
21. If the document appears to duplicate a record already processed today, append DEDUPE: check.
22. Watchlist policy: if any name in the document is an exact match for an entry on the watchlist, append a line FLAG: <name>. A similar or same-type name that is not on the list does not count. Watchlist: Brightlance Cohort, Langfield Junction, Oakford Platoon, Tarbet Station, Corporal Cavanagh.
23. Assign a ROUTE: GREEN (routine) or AMBER (needs review).
